response.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film WHERE rental_duration >= 5 GROUP BY rating), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS bench FROM per_rating WHERE avg_rate_per_day IS NOT NULL) SELECT p.rating, p.avg_rate_per_day, p.films, p.avg_rate_per_day / b.bench AS ratio_to_benchmark FROM per_rating p CROSS JOIN benchmark b WHERE b.bench IS NOT NULL;

assumptions.assumption: The benchmark is the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages for the rating groups that remain after filtering to rental_duration >= 5, so it is computed over the same films that are shown.
rental_rate and rental_duration are NOT NULL in the schema and rental_duration >= 5 excludes zero, so the division never yields NULL or divides by zero; AVG ignores any NULL per-film values anyway.

alternatives.interpretation: The benchmark is the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages across all ratings in the full film table, before the rental_duration >= 5 filter is applied; the per-rating rows still use only films with rental_duration >= 5.
alternatives.sql: WITH all_ratings AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day FROM film GROUP BY rating), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS bench FROM all_ratings WHERE avg_rate_per_day IS NOT NULL), per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS films FROM film WHERE rental_duration >= 5 GROUP BY rating) SELECT p.rating, p.avg_rate_per_day, p.films, p.avg_rate_per_day / b.bench AS ratio_to_benchmark FROM per_rating p CROSS JOIN benchmark b WHERE b.bench IS NOT NULL;
